conceptual assets.information: The runtime enable setting determines whether the clock-divider engine advances and produces clock-enable pulses on which downstream operation depends. It enters through enable_i and is held in en; no output carries the setting itself.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The setting is configuration material copied into en and used to control counter operation, so changing enable_i can alter clock generation (lines 129-134). Clearing enable_i makes en low, clears cnt, and withholds the generated clock-enable pulses needed by dependent logic (lines 129-134, 140-147).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could drive enable_i low or toggle it unexpectedly, clearing or altering the divider and disrupting dependent logic.

conceptual assets.information: The divided clock-enable pulse set on clk_en_o controls the timing and release of downstream clocked logic. It is generated internally from divider state, so no input port carries the pulse information itself.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: These outputs are critical control information, and changing the enable-controlled divider behavior can produce an incorrect downstream pulse schedule (lines 129-147). If the divider is disabled, cnt is cleared and the output pulse set is withheld, which can stall dependent logic (lines 129-140).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the clock-enable generation control so that pulses are mistimed or absent, causing dependent logic to operate incorrectly or stop.

considered, not kept.reason: The reset inputs, release registers, synchronized reset copies, and reset outputs only combine, gate, register, or pass reset chains, which the clock/reset exclusion bars (lines 44-73).
cnt and cnt2 are divider state used only to pace and generate the clock-enable pulses, so the pacing-state rule bars them as a separate conceptual asset (lines 131-147).
NUM_EN and the fixed divider selections only determine the build-time structure or fixed output choices and cannot be changed or withheld at run time (lines 102-104, 140-147).
